examples.en: A small stream runs through the middle of the city.
Children are splashing in the stream.
When it rains, the stream swells.
I walked along the path beside the stream.

examples.ko: 개천 물이 맑아서 작은 물고기가 보여요.
examples.en: The stream water is clear, so I can see small fish.
Cherry blossoms bloomed along the stream.

explain: '강'보다 작고 '시내', '냇물'과 비슷한 곳을 가리켜요. 도시에서는 '청계천'처럼 '천'이 붙은 이름이 많고, 말할 때는 '개천'이 가장 쉬운 말이에요.

phrases.example: 가난한 집 아이가 의사가 되다니, 개천에서 용 났네요.
phrases.en: A dragon rises from the stream.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어려운 환경에서 훌륭한 사람이 나왔다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said when someone from a humble background becomes very successful.

explain_en: It is smaller than a '강' and close to '시내' and '냇물'. In cities many streams have names ending in '천', like '청계천', but in speech '개천' is the easiest word.

examples.en: There is a spider web in the corner of the window.
Morning dew glistened on the spider web.

examples.ko: 오랫동안 안 쓴 창고에는 거미줄이 가득했어요.
examples.en: The storage room, unused for a long time, was full of cobwebs.
I swept away the cobwebs with a broom.
A small bug got caught in the web.

examples.ko: 거미줄 모양 과자가 신기해서 사 봤어요.
examples.en: I bought a web-shaped snack because it looked interesting.

explain: 거미가 만든 줄이에요. 거미가 집을 짓는 것은 '거미줄을 치다', 사람이 걷어 내는 것은 '거미줄을 걷어 내다'라고 해요. 오래 안 쓴 곳을 말할 때 '거미줄이 쳐져 있다'고 자주 말해요.
explain_en: The spider spins its web with 거미줄을 치다, and a person clears it with 거미줄을 걷어 내다. A common phrase for a place left unused is 거미줄이 쳐져 있다.

examples.en: Long icicles hang from the edge of the eaves.

examples.ko: 아침 햇볕에 고드름이 녹아서 물이 떨어져요.
examples.en: The icicles melt in the morning sun and water drips down.
I can hear the sound of icicles melting and trickling.
The kids snapped off icicles and played with them.
Be careful, because falling icicles are dangerous.
When winter comes, icicles form on the roof.

explain: '고드름이 달리다, 얼다, 녹다'처럼 함께 써요. 손으로 떼어 낼 때는 '고드름을 따다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It pairs with '달리다', '얼다' and '녹다'. When you snap one off by hand, you say '고드름을 따다'.

examples.en: A pheasant suddenly flew up on the mountain path.
A pheasant's call can be heard loudly even from far away.
I saw a pheasant in the field.
In the past people sometimes made dumplings with pheasant meat.

examples.ko: 꿩 깃털로 장식한 모자를 박물관에서 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a hat decorated with pheasant feathers at the museum.
The kids were amazed to see a pheasant.

explain: 산이나 들에 사는 큰 새라서 도시에서는 보기 어려워요. 속담에도 자주 나오는 새예요. 아래 '이렇게도 써요'의 두 속담은 일상에서도 많이 말해요.

phrases.example: 이 방법이면 꿩 먹고 알 먹기예요.
phrases.en: This way, it's killing two birds with one stone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 가지 일로 이익을 두 가지 얻을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when one action brings two benefits.
phrases.en_equiv: kill two birds with one stone

phrases.example: 원하는 색이 없어서 꿩 대신 닭으로 다른 색을 샀어요.
phrases.en: The color I wanted was out, so I bought another color as a second best.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원하는 것이 없을 때 비슷한 다른 것으로 대신한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means settling for a similar substitute when the thing you want isn't available.

explain_en: It is a large bird that lives in mountains and fields, so it is hard to see in cities. It also shows up in proverbs. The two proverbs under '이렇게도 써요' are used a lot in daily life.

examples.en: Ants find their way with their antennae.
The butterfly's antennae quivered.
The snail pulled its feelers right in.

examples.ko: 곤충 더듬이는 냄새를 맡는 일도 해요.
examples.en: Insect antennae also help them smell.
I found an insect with long antennae in the field guide.
The child closely observed the bug's antennae.

explain: 곤충이나 달팽이 머리에 달려 주변을 느끼는 부분에 써요. '더듬다'에서 온 말이라 손으로 더듬듯 주변을 살핀다는 느낌이에요. 사람에게는 쓰지 않고 '더듬이가 길다/떨리다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is used for the part on the head of an insect or snail that senses its surroundings. It comes from '더듬다' (to grope), giving the feel of probing around like a hand. It isn't used for people; you say '더듬이가 길다/떨리다'.

examples.ko: 말벌에 쏘이면 크게 부을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you get stung by a hornet, it can swell up a lot.

examples.ko: 처마 밑에 말벌 집이 생겨서 무서웠어요.
examples.en: A hornet nest formed under the eaves, and I was scared.
Hornets are much bigger and more aggressive than honeybees.

examples.ko: 가을에 산에 갈 때는 말벌을 조심하세요.
examples.en: Be careful of hornets when you go to the mountains in autumn.

examples.ko: 말벌이 방 안으로 들어와서 창문을 열었어요.
examples.en: A hornet came into the room, so I opened the window.
The firefighters were dispatched because of hornets.

explain: '꿀벌'은 꿀을 모으는 순한 벌이고, 말벌은 몸집이 크고 독이 강한 벌이에요. 가을에 산에 가면 말벌 주의 안내가 자주 나와요. 벌에 쏘이는 건 '벌에 쏘이다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: 꿀벌 is the gentle bee that collects honey, while 말벌 is a large hornet with strong venom. Warnings about 말벌 often appear in autumn when people go hiking. Getting stung by a bee is said as 벌에 쏘이다.

examples.en: The kids are kicking a ball on the bare ground.
It rained, so the bare ground became muddy.
If you sit on the bare ground, your bottom gets cold.
The playground was bare ground with not a blade of grass.
This flower grows well even on bare ground.
It was hard to pitch a tent on the bare ground.

explain: 풀이나 바닥재 없이 흙이 그대로 드러난 땅이에요. 집 안 바닥에는 보통 '맨바닥'을 쓰고, '맨땅'은 밖의 흙땅에 써요. '맨-'은 아무것도 덮이거나 더해지지 않았다는 뜻으로 '맨손, 맨발'에도 나와요.

phrases.example: 아무 경험 없이 가게를 열어서 맨땅에 헤딩하는 기분이에요.
phrases.en: I opened a shop with no experience, so it feels like I'm starting from nothing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 준비나 도움 없이 처음부터 무작정 부딪쳐 보는 상황에 써요. 주로 말할 때 쓰는 구어체예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you take on something from zero with no preparation or help. Mostly colloquial.
phrases.en_equiv: start from scratch; go in blind

explain_en: It is ground where the soil is exposed, with no grass or paving. For floors inside a building people usually say '맨바닥', while '맨땅' is for outdoor soil. The prefix '맨-' means nothing is covering or added, as in 맨손 and 맨발.

examples.ko: 산에서 멧돼지를 만나면 조용히 피해야 해요.
examples.en: If you meet a wild boar in the mountains, you should quietly avoid it.
A wild boar dug up the field, so the farmer is upset.

examples.ko: 멧돼지는 코로 땅을 파서 먹이를 찾아요.
examples.en: A wild boar digs the ground with its nose to find food.
I saw a baby wild boar at the zoo.
I climbed a tree to escape from the wild boar.
There is a kid who is as strong as a wild boar.

explain: 집에서 기르는 '돼지'와 달리 산에 사는 야생 돼지예요. '멧토끼', '멧새'처럼 '멧-'이 붙은 산에 사는 동물 이름도 있어요.
explain_en: Unlike the farm pig, this is a wild pig living in the mountains. Other mountain animals carry the same prefix, such as 멧토끼 (wild hare) and 멧새 (bunting).

examples.en: The cat hid in the thicket.
A strange sound came from the bushes by the road.

examples.ko: 비가 온 뒤라 수풀이 더 푸르러졌어요.
examples.en: After the rain, the thicket turned even greener.
We pushed through the thicket and walked ahead.
In summer, there are lots of bugs in the thicket.
The thicket is so overgrown that I can't see the path.

explain: '숲'은 나무가 많은 넓은 곳이고, 수풀은 풀과 나무가 빽빽하게 자란 곳이에요. '수풀 속에 숨다'처럼 작은 곳을 말할 때 어울리고, 일상에서는 '숲'이 훨씬 자주 나와요.
explain_en: 숲 is a broad area with many trees, while 수풀 is a dense growth of grass and shrubs, fitting small spots as in 수풀 속에 숨다. In daily talk 숲 is much more common.

en: to be very dark; to be pitch-dark

examples.ko: 방 안이 너무 컴컴해서 아무것도 안 보여요.
examples.en: The room is so dark that I can't see anything.
When evening came, the alley turned dark.
It's scary to walk alone on a dark road.

examples.ko: 정전이 돼서 집 안이 온통 컴컴해요.
examples.en: There's a power outage, so the whole house is pitch-dark.
When I turned off the light, the room turned dark.

examples.ko: 터널 안은 컴컴해도 전조등을 켜면 괜찮아요.
examples.en: The tunnel is dark, but it's fine if you turn on the headlights.

explain: '캄캄하다'와 모음만 달라서 어감이 더 크고 묵직해요. '어둡다'보다 훨씬 깜깜한 느낌이고, '어두컴컴하다'처럼 합쳐서도 써요. 변화는 '컴컴해지다'로 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It differs from '캄캄하다' only in vowels and sounds bigger and heavier. It feels much darker than '어둡다' and also appears in '어두컴컴하다'. Change is often said as '컴컴해지다'.

examples.ko: 여름밤에는 풀숲에서 곤충 소리가 크게 들려요.
examples.en: On summer nights, loud insect sounds come from the grass thicket.
The ball rolled into the tall grass.

examples.ko: 풀숲을 헤치고 들어가 보니 작은 연못이 있었어요.
examples.en: When I pushed through the thicket, there was a small pond.

examples.ko: 풀숲에는 모기가 많으니까 긴 바지를 입으세요.
examples.en: There are many mosquitoes in the bushes, so wear long pants.
The cat disappeared into the bushes.

examples.ko: 키 큰 풀숲 속에 새 둥지가 있었어요.
examples.en: There was a bird's nest in the tall grass.

explain: 나무가 많은 '숲'과 달리, 풀이 빽빽하게 자란 곳에 써요. '수풀'과 비슷하게 쓰는데 일상 대화에서는 '풀숲'이 더 흔히 들려요. 벌레나 작은 동물이 숨는 곳으로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Unlike '숲', which has many trees, '풀숲' is a place where grass grows thickly. It is used much like '수풀', and in everyday talk '풀숲' is the one you hear more. It often appears as a hiding place for insects and small animals.
